### Security
- Clother is built with Go 1.27.2. v3.0.11 was built with Go 1.23, which no longer gets security fixes: `govulncheck` finds 35 reachable standard library vulnerabilities in it, and none in this release
- `clother test` and `clother bench` no longer follow redirects. Go drops `Authorization` on a cross-host redirect but keeps `x-api-key`, so for Kimi Code and the other providers that take `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY`, a 302 from the endpoint sent your key to whatever host it named
- `clother bench` masks your API key when a provider echoes it back in an error message
- `clother update` and `scripts/install.sh` only download over https (plain http is accepted for loopback origins only), refuse a redirect from https to http or from GitHub to another host, cap download sizes, and refuse an archive whose `clother` entry is not a regular file
- Releases can now be signed: `clother update` verifies an ed25519 (minisign) signature of `checksums.txt` before it trusts the checksum. No key is embedded yet, so on the default GitHub origin a missing signature only prints a warning. A release origin set through `CLOTHER_UPDATE_URL` or `CLOTHER_RELEASE_BASE_URL` is refused when Clother cannot authenticate the release, unless `CLOTHER_ALLOW_UNSIGNED_ORIGIN=1`
- `scripts/install.sh` refuses to install when no SHA-256 tool is available instead of skipping the check, matches the checksum on the exact asset name, and cannot run half-downloaded. `clother.sh` only fetches it over https
- `secrets.env` is opened without following symlinks, and Clother's config, data and cache directories are created `0700`. Masked keys show their last four characters only
- The CI and release workflows pin every action to a commit SHA, and only the job that publishes the release can write to the repository

### Fixes
- `clother uninstall` deleted `<bin>/claude` whatever it was and ran a recursive delete on the directories named by `CLOTHER_CONFIG_DIR`, `CLOTHER_DATA_DIR` and `CLOTHER_CACHE_DIR`: pointed at `~/Documents`, it wiped it. It now lists what it is about to remove, deletes only the launchers and files Clother created, keeps a directory that holds anything else, refuses your home directory and the filesystem root, and puts back the `claude` binary that `clother install` moved aside
- `clother install` no longer deletes a real binary that sits where a launcher or the `claude` shim goes: it is moved to `claude-real` or `<name>.bak`. Symlinks are replaced atomically, so a launcher never disappears from `PATH`
- A corrupted `launchers.json` can no longer make Clother delete files outside its bin directory
- `clother update` exits with an error when the new version cannot be downloaded or verified, instead of printing "installed" for the version already there
- Under Homebrew on Linux, launchers point to the stable `bin/clother` rather than the versioned Cellar path that `brew upgrade` removes
- Relative `PATH` entries are ignored when looking for the real `claude`, and file names are compared case-sensitively
- `clother test` reports an invalid base URL instead of crashing
- A value saved in `secrets.env` with surrounding double quotes no longer loses them on the next read
- Config files are flushed to disk before they replace the old ones, so a crash right after `clother config` cannot leave an empty `secrets.env`
- `clother bench` no longer cuts a preview or an error in the middle of a character

### Docs
- README: how updates are verified, what `clother uninstall` removes, and `CLOTHER_ALLOW_UNSIGNED_ORIGIN` for local release testing
